cues.text: A Shepherd Turned Dominican
Born Antonio Ghislieri in 1504 to a poor noble family at Bosco, near Alessandria in Lombardy, the future pope worked as a shepherd in his early youth.
The Dominicans of Voghera then took him in, recognizing his ability and providing him a solid education.
He entered the order, was ordained in 1528, and spent sixteen years teaching theology and philosophy before serving as prior of several Dominican houses.
Grand Inquisitor to Pope
Ghislieri's reputation for austere, uncompromising orthodoxy led to his appointment as inquisitor for Como and Bergamo, and by 1551 as commissary general of the Roman Inquisition.
Made a bishop in 1556, a cardinal in 1557, and grand inquisitor in 1558, he was elected pope in January 1566, taking the name Pius V .
Implementing Trent
Pius V devoted his pontificate above all to the rigorous implementation of the reforms decreed by the recently concluded Council of Trent .
He published a new, standardized Roman Catechism and a revised Breviary.
In 1570, he issued the reformed Roman Missal.
Promulgated by the bull Quo Primum , it would remain the standard form of the Latin Mass for the following four centuries.
He also commissioned a revision of the Vulgate and declared St. Thomas Aquinas a Doctor of the Church.
Reforming Clergy and Curbing Scandal
Working closely with his friend St. Charles Borromeo , Pius V pressed bishops to reside personally in their dioceses rather than governing from afar.
He insisted cardinals live simply and worked to raise standards of clerical discipline and public morality across the Papal States, including efforts to curb prostitution and ban bullfighting.
The Holy League and Lepanto
Alarmed at the advance of Ottoman naval power in the Mediterranean, Pius V worked tirelessly to forge the Holy League of Catholic powers.
It comprised Spain, Venice, and the Papal States, whose combined fleet, under Don John of Austria, won the decisive Battle of Lepanto in October 1571.
Pius attributed the victory to the Rosary and instituted an annual commemoration that his successor formalized as the Feast of the Holy Rosary.
Legacy
Pius V died in 1572, having reigned barely six years but leaving an outsized mark on the Catholic Church for centuries afterward.
The Tridentine liturgy, catechism, and clerical reforms he standardized remained essentially unchanged well into the twentieth century.
Canonized in 1712, he is remembered as one of the most consequential and uncompromising reforming popes in Church history.
